mcq.question: Which property makes `compute_bill` a pure function?

options.B: Its result depends only on its arguments and it changes nothing outside itself
options.C: It returns a struct instead of a number

mcq.explanation: Purity means no side effects (no printing, no globals, no I/O) and no hidden inputs. That is what makes it trivial to test and safe to reuse.

mcq.question: Why is `total_from_printed_bill` a warning sign rather than a solution?

options.A: Parsing text is not possible in C++
options.B: It is slower than recalculating the bill
options.C: Printed numbers are always rounded incorrectly
options.D: Reusing data by parsing printed text breaks whenever the presentation changes

mcq.explanation: Text output is for humans. When a program has to read it back, presentation and logic are coupled, and a harmless wording change becomes a bug.

bonus.question: Logging is a side effect too. How would you add logging to `compute_bill` without losing the benefits of a pure function?
Write a failing test for `format_bill_csv(const Bill&)` that produces one CSV line per bill, then implement it without changing `compute_bill` at all.
